nodes.body: Maya and her dad were at the park on a windy day. A big red balloon was tied to Maya's wrist with a droopy bow. It bobbed and tugged at her, dancing in the breeze like it wanted to play. Maya skipped down the path to show the ducks by the pond.

Whoosh! A big gust of wind swooshed right by them. The droopy bow wiggled and wiggled loose. The red balloon slipped off Maya's wrist and floated up, up, up, just past her fingertips. Dad grabbed her hand. "Quick!" he said. "Let's follow it!"

They trotted as fast as they could after the red balloon. It bounced along on the wind, round and bright against the blue sky. It bobbed and danced ahead of them down the path, heading toward the spot where the park path split into two.

choices.label: Run to where the path splits.

nodes.body: At the fork, the balloon hung in the air as if it was choosing too. The left path went down and around to the pond. The breeze tugged the balloon that way, low and tempting. The right path went up to the sunny hill. A gust pushed the balloon high that way.

choices.label: Follow it down to the pond.

nodes.body: Down by the pond, the balloon skimmed low over the water. Its string trailed behind like a little tail. The ducks went quack and quack, paddling after it in a bumpy line. The balloon drifted toward the tall reeds at the pond's edge.

Maya and Dad hurried along the bank while the ducks paddled right beside them, quack quack quack, a happy cheer. The balloon got closer and closer to the reeds. Up ahead, the string caught tight in the tall green reeds.

The balloon bobbed above the reeds, its string tangled out of reach over the water. Stepping stones led out toward the willow tree. A girl in a little boat waved from near the shore. Maya got to pick how to get close to her balloon.

Holding Dad's hand tight, Maya tiptoed from stone to stone. Splish, steady, splish. The ducks watched like they were in an audience. At the last stone, the balloon bobbed in the willow tree's twigs, right above her head.

The string of the balloon was looped loosely on a bendy twig, just a little too high. Dad spotted a stick by the bank. The breeze kept puffing at the leaves. Maya could reach up with the stick, or wait for the breeze to help.

choices.label: Wait for the breeze to help.

nodes.body: Dad held Maya steady while she stretched the stick way, way up. The tip nudged the loop of string. It slid down the twig, closer and closer to her open hand.

The string dropped right into Maya's hand. Got it! She wound it twice around her wrist and Dad tied the bow extra tight. The ducks quacked hooray and the willow tree seemed to wave. Maya and Dad walked home with the balloon bouncing proudly beside them.

Maya and Dad sat still on the last stone and watched. The breeze puffed once, twice, and the string slipped free of the twig. But instead of coming down, the balloon floated gently out over the lily pads.
The balloon drifted down and landed softly on the lily pads, round and red like a little boat. One by one the ducks paddled over to it, circling it slowly, as if meeting a brand new friend.

The ducks paddled in a proud circle around the red balloon, quack quack quack, a happy song. The littlest one bobbed beside it like a tiny guard. Maya giggled and waved from the stones. Her balloon had become the leader of the parade. That felt like a happy trade.
The girl glided her little boat to the bank and helped Maya and Dad aboard. Everyone held on snug. Out on the pond, the red balloon bobbed low over the water, its string dancing on the ripples.
They pedaled and pedaled, splish splash splish. The ducks raced alongside like an escort. The balloon skipped ahead on the breeze, straight toward the fountain in the middle of the park.

The fountain sprayed a cool silver mist. The balloon bounced softly on top of it, boing, boing, like the fountain was juggling it. Then it rolled down the spray, sliding closer and closer to the boat.

Plop! The balloon rolled right off the spray and landed in Maya's open arms, cool and misty. The girl cheered and the ducks quacked hooray. They pedaled back to shore with the balloon riding in Maya's lap like a round red captain.

Up the hill they went, puff puff. The balloon climbed higher too, a round red dot against the white clouds. From partway up, Maya heard bells ringing on the hillside. She saw children swooping kites at the very top.
The bells came from an ice cream cart with a big umbrella, parked on the hillside. Above it, the children flew their swooping kites. The balloon wobbled in between them, not knowing which way to go.

The balloon dipped low toward the ice cream cart, then bobbed up toward the kite flyers at the top. It could not make up its mind. Dad squeezed Maya's hand. "You get to pick," he said. "Which way should we try?"

choices.label: Run to the ice cream cart.
Climb up to the kite flyers.

nodes.body: Just as they reached the cart, the balloon bumped softly against the umbrella pole and its string wrapped around once. The ice cream man looked up from scooping and smiled. "What a new balloon customer!" he said.

choices.label: Look up at the tangled string.

nodes.body: The string was wound around the pole up where the umbrella spread, too high for Maya to reach. The ice cream man was very tall. Behind the cart, he kept a little stool. Maya could ask him to reach it, or climb the stool and try.

choices.label: Ask the ice cream man to reach it.

nodes.body: The ice cream man wiped his hands, stood on his tiptoes, and unwound the string. One loop, two loops. He caught the balloon before it could wiggle away and bowed like a fancy waiter.

The ice cream man handed Maya the balloon like it was the fanciest sundae on the menu. He added one small strawberry scoop. Maya tied the string tight, licked her cold ice cream, and grinned at Dad. What a delicious rescue!
Maya climbed the stool while Dad held her steady. She stretched way up on her tiptoes and her fingertips just brushed the very end of the dangling string. Almost, almost.
Right then a big wind swooped over the hill. The string spun loose off the pole and hopped past Maya's fingers. The balloon sailed up and away over the treetops, smaller and smaller.

Maya's chin wobbled as the red dot winked away behind the trees. The ice cream man said a balloon chaser deserves a red treat. He handed her a strawberry cone. Dad hugged her close. The ice cream was sweet and cold, and next park day they would pick a new balloon.
At the hilltop, the balloon rose in among the kites, bobbing like a round red kite that lost its tail. A kite girl named Emma grinned. "My kite can help!" she said. "Will you let me try?"
Emma let out string and her kite swooped up beside the balloon. Its long ribbon tail twirled gently around the string, soft as a hug, and held on tight.
Hand over hand, Maya and Emma wound the reel together. Down came the kite and the balloon, spinning slowly like leaves. Lower and lower, until the string brushed Maya's hands.

Maya held the balloon at last. Emma took back her clever kite. All the children cheered from the hilltop. Dad tied the string with a double bow. Maya and her brand new friend flew one more kite before going home.
